aws_bridge.title: Connect the Alexa (AWS IoT) bridge
aws_bridge.description: Configure the optional Alexa/AWS IoT bridge. Enter the endpoint hostname and select the three files downloaded for your AWS IoT Thing. Each file is checked and copied into Home Assistant’s private OverKill Smart Hub folder. After this page, you will choose Local, Cloud, or Both for MQTT transport.

data_description.aws_endpoint: Copy the endpoint hostname from AWS IoT Core → Settings. Do not include https:// or a path.
data_description.aws_client_id: Use a unique client ID allowed by the AWS IoT policy attached to this certificate. Do not reuse nodered-1 while Node-RED is connected, because MQTT brokers disconnect clients that share an ID.
data_description.aws_ca_pem: Select AmazonRootCA1.pem. This is the AWS root certificate, not your device certificate.
data_description.aws_cert_pem: Select the certificate generated for this AWS IoT Thing (often ends in .pem.crt).
data_description.aws_key_pem: Select the matching private key for the Thing (often ends in .pem.key). Keep this file private.

mqtt_transport.title: MQTT transport setup
mqtt_transport.description: Choose how OverKill hubs reach Home Assistant. Local uses the MQTT integration already configured in Home Assistant. Cloud uses a separate broker connection for hubs away from your LAN. Both enables local discovery and the cloud broker.

mqtt_cloud.title: Cloud MQTT broker details
mqtt_cloud.description: Enter the broker used by hubs outside your LAN. The ESP firmware uses plain MQTT, without TLS. Leave optional client ID and login fields blank if your broker does not require them. IMPORTANT: Cloud MQTT is unencrypted in the current firmware and integration. Nabu Casa secures Home Assistant remote UI access, but it does not protect this separate MQTT connection. Do not use Cloud/Both MQTT over the public Internet; use a VPN/private routed network until both MQTT clients support TLS.

mqtt_both.title: Cloud MQTT broker details for Local + Cloud mode
mqtt_both.description: Local MQTT discovery stays enabled. Enter the broker for hubs outside your LAN. The ESP firmware uses plain MQTT, without TLS. IMPORTANT: Cloud MQTT is unencrypted in the current firmware and integration. Nabu Casa secures Home Assistant remote UI access, but it does not protect this separate MQTT connection. Do not use Cloud/Both MQTT over the public Internet; use a VPN/private routed network until both MQTT clients support TLS.

confirm_hub.title: Add discovered OverKill hub?
confirm_hub.description: Found {hub_name} on {transport}. MQTT topic prefix: {topic_prefix}. Press Submit to add this hub to Home Assistant, or cancel this dialog to skip it. The chip tag and final device name will be corrected automatically when the hub publishes its identity.

data.bridge_entry_id: Alexa account / AWS bridge for this hub

data_description.bridge_entry_id: Select the Alexa account that should receive this hub’s learned devices. Choose None (no Alexa bridge) to keep the hub out of every Alexa catalogue. Remote/cloud hubs require an explicit selection to prevent accidental cross-account exposure.

discover_hub.title: Search for your OverKill hub
discover_hub.description: The selected MQTT transport is configured. Searching for retained hub discovery messages now. If no hub appears, make sure the hub is powered on and connected to the selected broker, then press Submit to search again.

existing_setup.title: OverKill Smart Hub setup options
existing_setup.description: Choose whether to add another independent Alexa/AWS bridge or update the shared MQTT transport settings.

data.setup_action: What would you like to configure?

assign_existing_hub.title: Assign an existing hub to the new bridge
assign_existing_hub.description: Optionally move one already-configured hub to {bridge_name}. This replaces its current Alexa catalogue assignment; other hubs remain with their existing bridge.

initial_setup.title: Set up OverKill Smart Hub
initial_setup.description: Start with MQTT-only control, or configure the optional AWS IoT bridge for Alexa now. Local MQTT setup does not require AWS certificates. You can add the AWS bridge later.

error.invalid_cert: A PEM file is missing or invalid. See the log for which one.
error.invalid_ca_file: Could not read a valid Amazon Root CA certificate. Select AmazonRootCA1.pem and check the file contents.
error.invalid_device_cert: Could not read a valid AWS IoT device certificate. Select the certificate for your Thing.
error.invalid_private_key: Could not read a valid private key. Select the matching private key for your Thing.
error.hub_not_found: No hub was detected yet. Check that the hub is online and connected to this MQTT broker, then press Submit to search again.

abort.transport_updated: MQTT transport updated. The integration has been reloaded.
abort.invalid_transport_mode: Select Local, Cloud, or Both for MQTT transport.
abort.setup_failed: The bridge or MQTT transport could not be configured. Check the Home Assistant logs and try again.
abort.setup_complete_hub_exists: Bridge and MQTT transport are configured. A hub is already configured, so no duplicate hub was added.
abort.bridge_added: The additional Alexa AWS bridge was added. Newly discovered hubs can be assigned to it during hub confirmation, or existing hubs can be reassigned in their options.
abort.bridge_hub_assigned: The hub was assigned to the new Alexa bridge. Its catalogue will be published to that bridge after the hub finishes syncing.

data.bridge_entry_id: Alexa account / AWS bridge for this hub

broker.title: Cloud broker details
broker.description: Enter the connection details for the cloud MQTT broker. The ESP firmware uses plain MQTT — no TLS.

error.invalid_endpoint: AWS IoT endpoint hostname is required.
error.already_configured: That AWS IoT endpoint is already used by another bridge. Use a separate AWS endpoint for each Alexa account.

rediscover_hubs.name: Rediscover hubs
rediscover_hubs.description: Re-subscribe to hub discovery topics and rebuild the hub list from retained MQTT messages.
